verses.text: The apostles and brothers throughout Judea soon heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers took issue with him
and said, "You visited uncircumcised men and ate with them."
But Peter began and explained to them the whole sequence of events:
"I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision of something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.
I looked at it closely and saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.
Then I heard a voice saying to me, 'Get up, Peter, kill and eat.'
'No, Lord,' I said, 'for nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
But the voice spoke from heaven a second time, 'Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.'
This happened three times, and everything was drawn back up into heaven.
Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.
The Spirit told me to accompany them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man's home.
He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, 'Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.
He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.'
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.
Then I remembered the word of the Lord, as He used to say, 'John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'
So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?"
When they heard this, their objections were put to rest, and they glorified God, saying, "So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life."
Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the message only to Jews.
But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.
The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
and when he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. (This happened under Claudius.)
So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.
This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.

context.author: Traditionally Luke, the physician and traveling companion of Paul
context.genre: Historical narrative — the early church's story, with speeches and eyewitness travel reports
context.audience: Theophilus, and through him a Greek-speaking readership of Jews and Gentiles
context.setting: Peter returns to Jerusalem and defends his visit to a Gentile home. Meanwhile believers who fled after Stephen's death reach Antioch in Syria and speak to Greeks as well as Jews. Barnabas goes there from Jerusalem, fetches Saul from Tarsus, and teaches the new church for a year. At Antioch the disciples are first called Christians.
context.custom: "Christians" (v.26) is probably a name given by outsiders, a Greek word with a Latin-style ending meaning "followers of Christ." Antioch was the third largest city of the Roman world, a major crossroads with a mixed population. A famine during the reign of Claudius, around AD 46-48, is also mentioned by ancient historians.
context.timelineImmediate: The Antioch church sends relief to Judea and then, in chapter 13, sends out Barnabas and Saul. Antioch becomes the base for missionary work to the Gentile world.
context.timelineBible: When Peter reports that the Spirit fell on the Gentiles, the church recalls Jesus' words, "John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit" (v.16, from 1:5). The Gentile conversions fulfill Joel 2:28 and Isaiah 49:6, where salvation reaches the ends of the earth.
context.sparkNotes: Peter explains why he ate with Gentiles, and the Jerusalem church praises God. The gospel spreads to Antioch, where Barnabas and Saul teach a growing, mixed church. The disciples are first called Christians, and they send help to believers in Judea during a famine.

translation.meaning: Formed from Christos with a Latin-style ending meaning "people of." It appears only three times in the New Testament (here, 26:28, and 1 Peter 4:16).

otBackground.note: The Spirit is poured out on everyone, as Peter recalls.
The light to the nations reaches Antioch.
Foreigners who join the Lord are welcomed to his house.

overview.summary: Peter defends the Gentile conversions in Jerusalem. At Antioch Barnabas and Saul teach a mixed church, where the disciples are first called Christians.

history.t: A great city on the Orontes river, home to a large Jewish community.
A food shortage under Emperor Claudius hit Judea hard.

customs.t: Jewish believers were wary of eating with uncircumcised Gentiles.
Each disciple gave according to his ability, a model for later churches.

archaeology.t: Roman villas in Antioch yielded splendid floor mosaics.
A long main street lined with columns ran through the city.

overview.discussion: Barnabas saw the grace of God and was glad. What would change if we looked for grace first in places we had not expected it?
overview.book: The book of Acts · 28 chapters. The story of how the good news about Jesus spread from Jerusalem to Rome.
overview.author: Luke
